title: Sign-rank bounds from constant margin
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
formal: For every real \(\rho \in\)(0,1], does there exist a finite integer \(d(\rho )\), independent of matrix dimensions, such that every finite sign matrix A with margin \(m(A)\ge \rho\) has sign-rank at most \(d(\rho )\)? This is the dimension-free bounding-function question written in the source as rank±\((A)\le \eta (m(A)^{- 1})\); no polynomial or computable bound on \(\eta\) is requested.
context:
Rows can be represented as points and columns as oriented hyperplanes through the origin. Sign-rank minimizes the ambient dimension; margin instead maximizes the smallest normalized separation from any hyperplane.

The source recalls a bound of order \(m(A)^{- 2}\log  N\) for an \(N\times N\) matrix. The open question is whether any dependence on N can be removed, even at the cost of an arbitrarily worse dependence on margin.

Small sign-rank need not imply a large margin. Thus the card concerns the particular direction from a positive margin lower bound to bounded dimension.

The later theorem shows that exact k-Hamming-distance matrices have sign-rank bounded by \(2^{O(k)}\), independently of input length. It refutes the particular growing-rank conjecture proposed alongside Question 1.4, while restating the general question as open.

The April 2026 work obtains strong lower bounds for a Gap Hamming Distance promise problem. Its matrix leaves intermediate distances unspecified, so it does not give a fully specified constant-margin counterexample to the present statement.
why: Asks whether robust high-dimensional point–halfspace representations can always be replaced by bounded-dimensional representations, connecting geometric learning parameters with communication complexity.
status_note: The primary definitions and question were matched to the explicit open restatement in the March 2026 conference-version revision. April 2026 partial-matrix progress was checked separately. No total-matrix resolution was located through 12 September 2026.

progress.text: The source presents the qualitative margin-to-sign-rank bound as Question 1.4 and separately conjectures growing sign-rank for a hypercube family.
The Hamming-distance family is proved to have constant sign-rank for fixed distance, refuting that proposed counterexample.
The revised conference version still explicitly asks the full margin-versus-sign-rank question.
New topological lower bounds treat partial Gap Hamming Distance matrices, not a total constant-margin counterexample.

Its margin measures how far every point stays from every relevant hyperplane after normalization.
Its sign-rank is the smallest dimension of any representation with the correct signs.
The question asks whether a fixed positive margin forces a dimension bound independent of matrix size.
Recent work disproves a proposed Hamming-distance counterexample but explicitly leaves the general question open.

definitions: A sign matrix \(A\in \{- 1,+1\}^{r\times s}\) has positive finite numbers r,s of rows and columns and has every entry specified. Its sign-rank rank±\((A)\) is the least \(D\ge 1\) for which there are unit vectors \(u_{1},\ldots ,u_{r},v_{1},\ldots ,v_{s}\in \mathbb{R}\)ᴰ with \(A_{ij}\langle u_{i},v_{j}\rangle >0\) for all i,j. Equivalently it is the minimum real rank of a matrix B satisfying \(A_{ij}B_{ij}>0\) entrywise; zero entries do not realize either sign. The margin \(m(A)\) is the supremum, over such unit-vector representations in all finite dimensions D, of \(\min _{i,j} A_{ij}\langle u_{i},v_{j}\rangle\). It lies in (0,1]. In optimizing margin, the representation dimension is unrestricted; the representation of least dimension need not maximize margin. The requested d may grow arbitrarily rapidly as \(\rho\) tends to zero, but for each fixed positive \(\rho\) it must bound all matrix sizes. Equivalently, one can use a finite nondecreasing bounding function \(\eta\):[\(1,\infty\))→\(\mathbb{N}\). This uniform bounded-margin interpretation is explicitly restated in the later source’s Open Problem 1.3. Matrices with missing or promise-restricted entries are excluded.
answer_criterion: Prove a finite size-independent bound \(d(\rho )\) for every positive margin threshold \(\rho\), or prove there is a fixed \(\rho >0\) and a sequence of fully specified finite sign matrices with margins at least \(\rho\) and unbounded sign-ranks. No efficient procedure for producing the low-dimensional representation is required. Unbounded sign-rank with margins tending to zero, or only for partial matrices, does not refute the statement.
